first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses both declining completion and activation, with two inherited findings supporting early adoption gains. Verify memory_86 to assess whether those gains translated into sustainable qualified revenue. Verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response to current competitive pressure but may carry unreported retention, margin, or customer-quality risks.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified record showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Signup simplification provides additional activation evidence. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal.

final2.rationale: Proceed with the onboarding experiment rather than react with discounting. Shortened onboarding previously improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, supporting sustainable revenue while addressing current activation and completion declines. Although the competitor’s deeper cut increases urgency, the verified 40% promotion produced 12% lower retention and cohorts that failed to survive first renewal. Other pricing designs could behave differently, but there is no verification capacity this cycle to test that uncertainty safely.
